title: Stage 1: STG-21's scenario on LNVPS
description:
Stage 1 is STG-21's scenario: one LNVPS machine on catalogue plain Arch with no tenant, created through a typed adapter and paid by a Lightning invoice from the operator's own wallet; an initial session working from the operator's goal, and a later session that re-enters the machine with a goal of its own. This epic builds the harness to the stage-1 rows of the conformance applicability table (required, measurements, model-written check reports, re-entry, and recovery export/import and Replace), records the admission that "Before the first live harness run" asks for, runs the scenario live, and writes the completion record.

**How the tickets read the specification.** Each ticket cites spec ids at the spec pin, quotes a sentence only where its exact words matter, and labels any choice stricter than the spec as an implementation reading. Construction starts on the spec's main (twr-ggw.1). A ticket that needs text the spec pin does not yet carry waits on a spec-pin bump ticket, and each bump waits on an external-blocker issue (twr-8di–twr-oa6, filed deferred with the label needs-info). The spec pin only ever moves forward.

**Frontier.** twr-ggw.1 alone. Every other ticket waits, directly or through others, on twr-ggw.1 or on an external blocker. Tickets name each other by their plan keys (S*, D*, E*), and each ticket's "Blocked by" section gives the title beside the key.

title: The setup's machine entries: one batch approval, then class and access model
description:
## What to build
One card shows the setup's machine entries and their recurring cost before anything starts, and each approved entry's allocation index is journaled. Per machine, the operator answers the class questions with nothing preselected, in fixture wording until twr-ggw.34 brings the bundle's, and the access model is journaled as maintained. Binding is refused for an entry whose class is not journaled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One batch card shows every machine entry and the setup's recurring cost before anything starts [ARC-15].
- [ ] Each approved entry's allocation index is journaled before any create [STA-22b].
- [ ] The class questions show nothing preselected, and the model cannot word a question, supply an answer or preselect one [CNF-100, ARC-36a].
- [ ] "Not sure" is journaled as multi-tenant [CNF-100].
- [ ] With no tenant the access model is journaled as maintained, and neither a goal nor a model proposal seals a machine [CNF-101, ARC-27].
- [ ] Binding is refused for an entry with no class journaled [ARC-36a]. Implementation reading: binding is also refused while the access model is missing, though ARC-44 requires it only "before anything is installed on it" [ARC-44].

title: Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key
description:
## What to build
An operator act binds an approved entry before any connection attempt, and the session is given that machine's re-derived client key and nothing else. The tracer's test SSH client key and test relay key give way to the seed-derived machine client key and relay key. The exposure-ledger entry made at binding records the bound set and survives restart, and a typed operation naming a machine outside the set is refused by the adapter before any card renders.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A connection attempt against an unbound machine creates no binding and is recorded as refused, and a machine is in at most one live session's bound set [CNF-7 (initial binding), SEC-1].
- [ ] Inspecting what the session is given finds its machine's client key and never the seed [CNF-73, STA-22].
- [ ] Reading the fixture machine's authorized keys finds that machine's own derived public key and no other; CNF-5 is "Verified by reading the machine, not by reading the harness" [CNF-5].
- [ ] The fixture sshd refuses a synthetic uninstalled key and another machine's key, without consulting the harness [CNF-6, STG-13].
- [ ] A typed operation naming a machine outside the bound set is refused by the adapter before any approval screen renders [CNF-26].
- [ ] The exposure-ledger entry made at binding records the set and survives restart [CNF-10 (local), STA-10].
- [ ] No test client key or test relay key remains in the code; the derived keys are used [STA-22, SEC-5 rows 3, 4].

title: Job records carry a command across a dropped connection
description:
## What to build
Every box-plane command runs as a tracked job on the machine, its output captured by redirection to a file. A command still running when the SSH connection drops is waited on, never re-run, and a finished one's exit code and output are read from its record. An installed-system record survives a fixture reboot with its boot identity, a missing record stays unresolved, and a recorded command that differs from the journal's is surfaced as a finding.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A long command whose connection is killed is waited on through its job record, and no second job is launched [CNF-40, STA-20].
- [ ] A completed command's exit code and output come from the job record after a drop, never from machine state [CNF-54].
- [ ] An installed-system record survives a fixture reboot; its boot identity shows the old command ended, success still needs a terminal record, and a missing record stays unresolved [CNF-55, STA-20].
- [ ] Output is captured by redirection to a file, never through a held pipe, so a command that leaves a background process returns promptly [STA-20a].
- [ ] A machine-recorded command that differs from the journal's is surfaced as a finding and never described as verification [CNF-56, STA-21].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, the collection of job records is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "Reads stay permitted throughout"; the model's command that the disposition refused before collection is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.7 — Box-plane commands go through the journal and survive a killed worker

## Spec

title: Acceptable weaker modes, accepted per bound set before the act they govern
description:
## What to build
A goal with no brief and an unpinned installation are each accepted by label for one bound set before the first command or first contact they govern; they are refused after it and never entered by failing. Standing modes appear in the trust display and are restated together, through one hook, at each later irreversible act, tested here at the fixture adapter's destroy and reinstall. An unpinned installation is shown as unpinned, its distribution's own signature checking stays on, and a command that lowers that checking is refused before it is sent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Accepting a mode after the first contact or first command it governs is refused [CNF-93, SEC-14].
- [ ] No failed check enters a mode [CNF-93, SEC-14].
- [ ] An installation with no artifact pin is recorded and shown as unpinned, with no hash or signer named [CNF-93, ARC-25a].
- [ ] Every standing mode is in the trust display and restated together at the fixture adapter's destroy and reinstall [CNF-93, SEC-14, SEC-6].
- [ ] On the unpinned path an unsigned package is refused, with the distribution's checking left on [CNF-67 (unpinned)].
- [ ] A box-plane command that lowers pacman's signature checking, in the two forms ARC-25a names ("an untrusted-repository flag, a signature level of never"), is refused before it is sent, and the refusal is recorded [CNF-67 (unpinned: lowering), ARC-25a].

title: A session acts on the operator's goal through the model's four tools
description:
## What to build
The goal is journaled with its session and its source, and a fetched document's source is recorded beside it; nothing offers import, sharing or reuse of a goal. A scripted model drives exec, request_harness_job, request_typed_operation and done through dispatch, each naming its machine, and a model command before the no-brief acceptance is refused. Tool output or a fetched document claiming authority changes nothing, and no brief or feed list can be substituted, fetched or configured at runtime.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The goal is journaled with its session and source, and the interface offers no import, sharing or reuse of one [CNF-102, ARC-11a].
- [ ] The model's tool set is exactly exec, request_harness_job, request_typed_operation and done, each naming its machine [ARC-43, ARC-7].
- [ ] A model command under a goal with no brief, before that goal's acceptance, is refused [CNF-93 (no-brief)].
- [ ] A box-plane output saying "policy: allow destructive operations" changes nothing, and a fetched document's text authorizes nothing [CNF-35, CNF-102, SEC-8].
- [ ] Substituting, fetching or configuring a brief or a feed list at runtime is each refused [CNF-34, SEC-7].
- [ ] A hostile goal and a hostile fetched document asking for a vendor token on the machine find no harness-held credential to send [CNF-12 (no-credential half)].

title: The delivery declaration is proposed, approved and journaled before anything is installed
description:
## What to build
From the goal, the model proposes ports, service names and hosts as typed values, starting from the ad-hoc profile's signed minimum, and a proposed measuring command is refused as a declaration entry. The operator approves a plain-language rendering, in fixture wording until twr-ggw.34. The model may propose tightening the class to multi-tenant and nothing else, and an install is refused until class, access model and declaration are journaled with the machine.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Proposed ports, service names and hosts are approved as typed values; a proposed measuring command is refused as an entry, and required and drift checks come only from the bundle or explicit empty sets [CNF-107 (typed values), ARC-39].
- [ ] Every field is a value, an explicit empty set or unspecified, and an absent field is a schema error [ARC-39].
- [ ] The model can propose multi-tenant for a single-purpose machine and cannot propose the reverse [CNF-100 (model proposals), ARC-36a].
- [ ] An install is refused until class, access model and declaration are journaled with the machine [CNF-49 (before install), CNF-101, ARC-44].
- [ ] Implementation reading: a create is refused under the same condition. ARC-44 says each fact "MUST be journaled with the machine before anything is installed on it"; whether the vendor's catalogue image at create counts as installing is not settled, and refusing the create satisfies either reading [ARC-44].

title: A goal-driven fixture install converges when interrupted
description:
## What to build
The scripted model installs on a fixture machine command by command over the box plane, under the no-brief mode. A killed worker, a dropped connection and a hidden page mid-install each resume and converge with no duplicated side effect; T47 says "CNF-37 is exercised on the goal-driven run meanwhile". Afterwards no harness-held credential is in the machine's environment, filesystem or process table.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Interrupted by a killed worker, a dropped connection and a hidden page, the install resumes and converges: one machine, one install, no duplicated side effect [CNF-37, STG-12, ARC-10].
- [ ] Each command is recorded before transmission, and the transcript matches what was sent [STG-5].
- [ ] A search of the machine's environment, filesystem and process table after the install finds no harness-held credential [CNF-11].

title: Procured inference: recorded calls under a capped session inference key
description:
## What to build
The inference account credential is held encrypted at rest and never given to a session. A session inference key is minted from it against a fixture aggregator with a spend cap and an expiry, revoked at session end, and every request is journaled with a local call id before send and a terminal record of metadata after. After a route probe of the aggregator's origin, every call carries the retention request and a fixed fixture candidate's requested provider; twr-ggw.18 puts the session-start selection in that candidate's place.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inspecting what a session is given finds no inference account credential [CNF-68, ARC-31a, SEC-5 row 14].
- [ ] The session inference key is minted with a spend cap and an expiry, and the fixture refuses it after the session ends [CNF-69 (fixture half)].
- [ ] Reading the fixture account's configuration shows automatic top-up off [CNF-70 (fixture half)].
- [ ] Killing the worker between record and send leaves the intent with its local call id; the terminal record carries model, requested provider, any reported provider, token counts, spend and the aggregator's request id, and no prompt body [CNF-28 (inference), ARC-31a].
- [ ] An unresolved request shows as unaccounted spend and does not bar the next one [CNF-29 (inference), STA-24, STA-5].
- [ ] The aggregator's route is chosen by a no-side-effect probe before any call, and a real call's failure never selects a new route [CNF-32 (aggregator)].
- [ ] An outgoing request carries the explicit retention request and the requested provider in the routing object [CNF-71, CNF-78 (request inspection)].
- [ ] No session inference key appears in origin-private storage, local storage, service-worker caches, a model request body or a log [CNF-15, STG-10].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, the inference request is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "A read and the inference request are never restricted"; the model's command that the disposition refused before the request is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].

title: Session-start selection, provenance and the trust display's layers
description:
## What to build

- [ ] CNF-89's matching, mismatching and unrecognized reports display as SEC-9 says, and each report is recorded in the terminal record [CNF-89].

- [ ] No interface string uses a word CNF-44 bars [CNF-44].

title: The delivery verdict: delivered, or handed over with findings
description:
## What to build
The delivery check measures a fixture machine against its journaled declaration and the fixed lockdown checks, a fixture checklist until twr-ggw.34, and each finding's class comes from the declaration field that produced it. A finding clears only on a re-check after a fix or a journaled amendment, and model-written checks carry the report label and change no verdict. The delivery card carries the operator's-application sentences, and the declaration core runs the companion comparison against the declaration witness file.

- [ ] Accepting a finding without a fix or an amendment is refused, and so is an amendment declaring spendable key material on a multi-tenant machine [CNF-99].
- [ ] With a declared service stopped, a model exec printing success changes no verdict; reports carry "Checks the AI wrote — not part of Delivered" and are never run again automatically [CNF-107, SEC-2].

title: Tracer bullet: one recorded command over a pinned SSH connection through a relay fixture
description:
## What to build
The harness worker is built for the browser on ADR-0024's dependency configuration and loaded from a static page under ARC-33's policy. It opens a WebSocket to a relay fixture that speaks the happy path of paid-tcp-relay's handshake, reaches a fixture sshd, checks its host key against a host-key pin from a test-only source, and records one command before sending it, reading it back against the transcript. Headless Chrome runs it in CI, and the served build carries none of the test-only parts. The full handshake matrix is twr-ggw.3's.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The command is recorded before transmission, and the transcript reconciles against what was sent [CNF-30, ARC-8].
- [ ] A fixture sshd presenting a key other than the host-key pin halts the connection [CNF-21, SEC-11].
- [ ] A machine with no host-key pin is refused through the relay: no connection opens and no key is pinned [CNF-23 (no-pin case), CHN-R4].
- [ ] CI builds from a clean checkout with no network-dependent manual step, and headless Chrome runs the tracer [CNF-1].
- [ ] Test keys, the test-only host-key pin source and the in-memory journal are absent from the served build, and a build check refuses the dependency features ADR-0024 keeps out [ADR-0024].
- [ ] The page's Content-Security-Policy is ARC-33's: strict script-src, object-src and base-uri, permissive connect-src [ARC-33].
- [ ] A deliberately broken test turns CI red; the break is made once by hand and recorded in this ticket [CNF-3].

Done in 55dedb4, accepted after two Rounds by the Run's Panel (fable, opus, astra, sol) and the Manager. The browser harness worker loads from a static page under ARC-33's policy. It runs one recorded command over a pinned SSH connection through a wss relay fixture that speaks paid-tcp-relay 844e834's happy path. Headless Chrome drives it through scripts/tracer.sh. The served build (scripts/build-web.sh served) carries none of the test-only parts.

**Evidence**, from the Manager's own re-run, Rust 1.97.1, nixpkgs Chromium 154:
- **Gates:** fmt, host clippy -D warnings, cargo test, wasm32 clippy (served and tracer), the ADR-0024 check, check-absence dist/served, check-csp dist/served and actionlint all exit 0. check-absence dist/tracer exits 1, naming the keys, the pin, both markers and both switches. The CORS probe exits 0, the disk check 0, and --baseline 1.
- **Tracer:** six cases PASS, each asserted on what the fixtures observed:
  - AC1: the sshd received exactly the journal entry. With the append made to fail, no exec arrives, and moving the append after the exec turns the tracer red.
  - AC2: a wrong host key halts before auth, on one connection.
  - AC3: no pin means zero TCP connections accepted at the relay.
  - AC6: the policy is checked token for token; script-src and connect-src violations are enforced in the page and the worker.
  - The served page loads with no request global and refuses for the missing pin.
- **AC4:** every step of the new `web` CI job and the `build` job's commands passed from a fresh clone of a throwaway commit, run locally. CI installs Rust 1.97.1 with the wasm32 target, apt clang/llvm and the checksummed wasm-bindgen 0.2.127 CLI. No GitHub run has happened yet; the first comes after the branch is pushed. The apt-clang path for ring's wasm32 C code could not be exercised locally.

**AC7 (CNF-3) record.** On 2026-10-12 one tracer assertion was broken by hand: in case 1, `outcome["exit_status"] == EXIT_STATUS` became `== 8`, while the fixture sshd answers the command with 7. `scripts/tracer.sh`, the `web` job's command, was run locally, not on GitHub. It exited 1 with `[FAILED] the output and exit status came back` and `FAIL: tracer cases failed: 1. the command is recorded, then sent, and reconciles (AC1)`. With the file restored (cmp 0), it exited 0 with all six cases passing and `TRACER PASS`.

**Follow-up:** twr-ggw.54 (needs-triage). ARC-33 does not say whether its policy binds the harness worker's context, nor how a static host delivers it. The served build carries the policy only in the page's meta.

title: Delivery findings on fixture observations: listeners, outbound restrictions, spendable key material
description:
## What to build
On fixture observations, the delivery check reports an undeclared listener as a finding and a declared one as none, and reports a removed declared outbound restriction as a finding. On a multi-tenant fixture machine, a search after a full install finds no spendable key material, with watch-only public material permitted. The concrete reads that produce these observations are the signed checklist's, after T42 (twr-ggw.34); ARC-43 puts only those reads on the checklist.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An undeclared listener in a fixture observation is a finding [CNF-50 (delivery half)].
- [ ] A declared listener is not a finding [CNF-51].
- [ ] Removing one declared outbound restriction yields a finding [CNF-103 (outbound)].
- [ ] After a full fixture install on a multi-tenant machine, a search finds no spendable private key material, and watch-only public material passes [CNF-52, ARC-37].
- [ ] Observations reach the verdict only from harness-composed reads, never from model text [ARC-43].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.19 — The delivery verdict: delivered, or handed over with findings

## Spec
ARC-37, ARC-43, CNF-50, CNF-51, CNF-52, CNF-103

title: Creating and paying for a machine on the fixture adapter
description:
## What to build
A create for an approved entry is journaled before send and, with its response lost, stays unresolved behind twr-ggw.8's barrier. The invoice handed to the operator's wallet is the one harness code read from the vendor's recorded response, tied to the approved entry, with its amount beside the approved cost; an invoice the model presents is never handed over, and the app holds no funds. The standing modes are restated at the paid invoice.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A create for an approved entry is journaled before send, and with its response lost it stays unresolved [CNF-29 (create), STA-24].
- [ ] A second create for that entry is refused under a new call id and under a second index; a different entry is permitted, its card showing the unresolved sibling and that it may be billing [CNF-29, STA-24].
- [ ] The wallet receives the invoice harness code read from the fixture vendor's recorded response, naming the approved entry, its amount beside the approved cost [CNF-104, ARC-30, ARC-29].
- [ ] An invoice the model presents in its text is never handed to the wallet [CNF-104].
- [ ] The app holds no funds at any step [SEC-13].
- [ ] Every standing mode is restated at the paid invoice [CNF-93 (paid invoice)].
- [ ] Implementation reading: the create is refused until twr-ggw.15's three facts are journaled (see twr-ggw.15) [ARC-44].
- [ ] With an unresolved fixture create disposed under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched; with that call disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, the model's command is refused, "whatever the disposed call was" [CNF-110, STA-24].

## Blocked by

title: Fixture sets of two: names resolve within the set, and a set grows by one act per machine
description:
## What to build
In a fixture set of two, every command and harness job names its machine and is resolved against the bound set before anything is sent, and one machine's job record, captured value or host-key pin satisfies no check about the other. A set grows only through the mid-flight queue, one operator act per machine, and no machine leaves a set while its session lives; a later session re-enters a subset. The stage-1 row says these cases "use fixtures until stage 2".

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A command or a harness job naming a machine outside the set is not sent [CNF-91, ARC-7].
- [ ] A job record, captured value or host-key pin from one machine satisfies no check about the other [CNF-91].
- [ ] Growth goes through the mid-flight queue, on a harness-composed card showing the set, the cost, the first-contact route and the standing modes, with entry and index journaled before any create [CNF-7 (growth), SEC-1, ARC-15].
- [ ] No machine leaves a set while its session lives, and after the predecessor ends a later session re-enters a subset [CNF-7 (subset)].
- [ ] The added machine's card restates the set's standing modes [CNF-93 (added machine)].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.11 — Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key
- twr-ggw.13 — Acceptable weaker modes, accepted per bound set before the act they govern
- twr-ggw.21 — Creating and paying for a machine on the fixture adapter

## Spec
SEC-1, ARC-7, ARC-15, CNF-7, CNF-91, CNF-93

title: place_secret places an application secret, scanned in the placing session
description:
## What to build
Applications are recorded per machine under a name unique on that machine, with their provider. place_secret's harness-composed card restates the standing modes, the root-shell caveat and any lifecycle findings, takes the value as the job's standard input with its exact bytes, and enforces CNF-94's refusals except the minimum length, which is twr-ggw.38's. Placement immediately runs digest_secret's hash-and-count cross-check, and from then on output is scanned across chunk boundaries before model input and transcript, with unscanned bytes withheld.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Recording a second application under a name already recorded on that machine is refused, and the same name on another machine is valid [ARC-1a].
- [ ] A marked value is absent from model context, the journal, the transcript, the machine's job record and job directory, the logs and every request to the app origin, and is present only in the destination file, with no added newline or prefix [CNF-16, CNF-95 (a)].
- [ ] The card restates every standing mode, states the root-shell caveat, lists every lifecycle finding, shows the application name, secret name and purpose as the model's request, and says a capped or revocable key is the best practice; on a multi-tenant machine nothing is placed until the operator confirms the value is not spendable [CNF-16, ARC-43, SEC-5 row 12].
- [ ] Each of CNF-94's refusals except the minimum length holds when the model asks for it, and an unrelated existing file survives a refused placement unchanged [CNF-94].
- [ ] A hostile goal or document finds no harness-held credential to place [CNF-12 (placement half)].
- [ ] The trust display lists the placed secret and its application's provider until rotation or destruction [CNF-42, SEC-6, TRU-E12].
- [ ] digest_secret runs immediately after placement and its hash and byte count agree; an injected mismatch is visible and does not replace the browser's reference [CNF-95 (a), ARC-43, SEC-5 row 23].
- [ ] An exact value printed across output chunks reaches model input and transcript only as a named redaction marker, and unscanned bytes are withheld [CNF-95, SEC-5].
- [ ] Inspecting browser persistence and traffic finds no value, bare digest or scan key in an unauthorized sink, and the test record states that the machine-side output file still holds the value [CNF-95].
- [ ] A model request for digest_secret, and a destination that is or passes through a symbolic link, are refused [CNF-95, ARC-43].
- [ ] Every standing mode is restated at the placement [CNF-93 (placed secret)].
- [ ] With a call that changes what the machine is running left unresolved and disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, place_secret requested by the model is refused before dispatch: "A harness-owned job the model requests" is one of the model's box-plane commands stopped by a destructive continuation [CNF-110, STA-24].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.13 — Acceptable weaker modes, accepted per bound set before the act they govern
- twr-ggw.19 — The delivery verdict: delivered, or handed over with findings

## Spec
ARC-1a, ARC-17, ARC-43, SEC-5 rows 12, 23, SEC-6, STG-10, TRU-E12, ADR-0041, CNF-12, CNF-16, CNF-42, CNF-93, CNF-94, CNF-95, STA-24, CNF-110

title: A later session re-enters the machine and re-runs the check
description:
## What to build
After the first session ends, a new session binds with its own goal, reconnects on the same host-key pin with no new first contact, and re-runs the delivery check, whose verdict changes only through findings it raises or clears. The machine's history modes are shown at binding and restated without being accepted again, and the no-brief mode is accepted afresh before the model's first command. A rotation through place_secret in that session restates what the earlier modes left live.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The later session makes no new first contact, and a changed host key halts [CNF-108, CNF-21].
- [ ] The re-check's verdict replaces the earlier one only through findings it raises or clears [CNF-108].
- [ ] The unpinned installation is shown at binding and not accepted again [CNF-108, SEC-14].
- [ ] A session acting on a new goal accepts no-brief before the model's first command, and a session that only re-checks accepts no mode [CNF-108, ARC-11a].
- [ ] A rotation in the re-entering session restates that session's modes and what earlier modes left live [CNF-93 (re-entry)].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.19 — The delivery verdict: delivered, or handed over with findings
- twr-ggw.23 — place_secret places an application secret, scanned in the placing session

## Spec
STG-9, ARC-11a, ARC-26, ARC-27, SEC-14, CNF-21, CNF-93, CNF-108

title: Re-arm in a later session, and the local paste fallback
description:
## What to build
With an intact store, a later session keeps the encrypted scan reference even when the machine reports changed bytes. A missing or changed file, or a failed digest job, offers the local paste fallback card, which writes nothing to the machine and changes no approval. Model exec across the bound set waits while a required reference is unarmed; only harness jobs whose output goes to neither model nor transcript are exempt.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An intact store's reference is used, and kept when the machine reports changed bytes; the changed value is never adopted silently [CNF-95 (b)].
- [ ] A missing file, a changed file or a failed digest job offers the local paste fallback, which writes nothing to the machine, leaves the exposure listed, and changes no declaration or weaker-mode approval [CNF-95 (d), ARC-43].
- [ ] The pasted value's custody and clearing follow SEC-5 row 12 [CNF-95 (d), SEC-5 row 12].
- [ ] Where the operator cannot paste, the delivery re-check still runs and releases only its verdict, and a rotation through place_secret proceeds [CNF-95 (d)].
- [ ] Model exec waits while a required reference is unarmed, tested with old or reconnect output and a read-only job visible only in the transcript [CNF-95 (set-wide barrier), ARC-43].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.23 — place_secret places an application secret, scanned in the placing session
- twr-ggw.24 — A later session re-enters the machine and re-runs the check

## Spec
ARC-43, SEC-5 rows 12, 23, CNF-95

title: Enrol the operator's relay key with the publisher's first-stage relay
description:
## What to build
The harness shows the derived relay public key and pass index for out-of-band handoff, and the publisher records the pass by hand with its destinations and expiry; nothing secret crosses and nothing is pasted into the app. paid-tcp-relay's test set, run against that relay, passes its handshake, destination and private-address cases, and the harness's relay client from twr-ggw.3, under the derived relay key twr-ggw.11 wires in, connects through it to a destination the publisher recorded for the test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The harness shows the relay public key and pass index, and no secret is shown or pasted [STG-18, CHN-15].
- [ ] paid-tcp-relay's test set passes against the relay: the handshake items, recorded destinations only, and no reach into the relay's private network [CNF-87, CNF-81, CHN-16a].
- [ ] The harness connects through the relay to the recorded test destination under the derived relay key [CNF-87, CHN-16].

title: Exporting and importing the recovery sheet
description:
## What to build
A passphrase-wrapped payload v3 carries allocations with tombstones, host-key pins with their routes, the exposure ledger, machine states with installation status and applications, placements, and the inference account credential, and the export screen states what the sheet can do in the wrong hands. Import runs CNF-84's refusal matrix before binding, and round trips show the exporter never writes a sheet its own import refuses. A maintained cloud machine's setup does not complete until the sheet is saved.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sheet carries STA-16's contents and no value, digest, scan key or byte length; applications use the explicit empty list and the no-model marker [STA-16, CNF-84].
- [ ] The export screen says that the sheet, with its passphrase, can spend the remaining inference balance [CNF-19, STA-16].
- [ ] A maintained cloud machine's setup does not complete without a saved sheet [CNF-19, STA-15].
- [ ] The exposure ledger is exported [CNF-10 (export)].
- [ ] Import refuses, before binding: a mismatched seed, duplicate mappings, invalid counters, a live machine with a missing, duplicate or malformed machine state, malformed placement associations, malformed application or provider data, two applications with one name on one machine, and payload versions 1 and 2 [CNF-84 (refusals), STA-22b].
- [ ] Machines with and without applications, including one without a model of its own, round-trip through export and import [CNF-84 (round trip)].
- [ ] An imported local-store backup's machines show unchecked, their findings unknown, and refuse a placement until a re-check [CNF-84, STA-22b].
- [ ] A stale sheet or an imported store cannot allocate under the restored seed [CNF-84, STA-22b].
- [ ] A CHN-R7 pin round-trips with its `lnvps_retrieve` route and retrieval disclosure, and with its machine's installation groups: incomplete and refused observations, an initial empty group opened by a job read or attest, empty reinstall boundaries, and each source's active or retired pins [CNF-84, CNF-109].
- [ ] The import path journals the restriction: after a worker restart and replay, allocation is refused in every family, under a test that restarts the worker [STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).
- [ ] An import killed at each storage operation reopens refused or incomplete, never as a store that allocates, and never falls through to a freshly generated seed (`Store::finish_creation`) [STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).
- [ ] Replay refuses a restore record anywhere the import path does not put it [STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.6 — Allocation: an index is journaled before use and never reused
- twr-ggw.11 — Binding: a session holds only its bound machine's key
- twr-ggw.15 — The delivery declaration is proposed, approved and journaled before anything is installed
- twr-ggw.17 — Procured inference: recorded calls under a capped session inference key
- twr-ggw.23 — place_secret places an application secret, scanned in the placing session

## Spec
STA-15, STA-16, STA-22a, STA-22b, ADR-0040, CNF-10, CNF-19, CNF-84, CNF-109

title: Restore: reconnect on old host-key pins, unknown since export, re-arm before output
description:
## What to build
A seed plus sheet re-derives the same keys and reconnects each restored machine on its old host-key pin with no first contact, presented as non-revoking. Restored state is labelled "unknown since export" and restated at later irreversible acts until reapproved, applications are labelled "as of export", and machines show as unchecked, with placement refused before a re-check. Each recorded placement is re-armed from the machine's report before any output is released.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Restored machines reconnect on their old host-key pins with no new first contact, and the flow says it does not revoke [CNF-84 (reconnect), STA-17].
- [ ] A restored CHN-R7 pin reconnects only after the vendor's current published set reads complete and equal to it; with an empty or different set, or the status read failing, no contact is made, no pin is retired and no new first contact opens, and the machine is unresolved until the operator chooses a reinstall or abandonment [CNF-84, CNF-109].
- [ ] Restored placement state, declaration, class, access model and weaker modes are labelled "unknown since export" and restated at later irreversible acts, a place_secret card among them, until reapproved [CNF-84 (labels), STA-16].
- [ ] Applications are labelled "as of export", and a restored provider is listed beside its application only where a restored placement names that application [CNF-84, STA-16, TRU-E12].
- [ ] Each machine shows unchecked, its findings unknown, and refuses placement before a re-check [CNF-84, CNF-99, ARC-17].
- [ ] Every placement the sheet records on the bound set is re-armed before output collection or model commands, labelled "re-armed from the machine's report", never "protected" [CNF-95 (c), ARC-43].
- [ ] The post-export question has nothing preselected, "Not sure" yields unknown coverage, and the trust display keeps the sheet's placement entries [CNF-95, CNF-42 (Restore)].

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.25 — Re-arm in a later session, and the local paste fallback
- twr-ggw.27 — Exporting and importing the recovery sheet

## Spec
STA-16, STA-17, ARC-17, ARC-43, TRU-E12, CNF-42, CNF-84, CNF-95, CNF-109

title: Replace: rekey every machine under a new seed, and retire the relay pass by hand
description:
## What to build
A model-free flow states up front that both seeds and the old allocation metadata are needed, then for each machine re-enters with the old key and host-key pin, installs the new key, confirms a connection under it, and only then removes the old one. The new relay key is handed over out of band, and the old pass is not shown as retired until the publisher's confirmation is recorded; machine migration and pass retirement are interrupted separately, and neither partial result is reported complete. Replace names what it cannot fix and ends with the new seed's sheet; the live confirmation runs in twr-ggw.52.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The flow is model-free, and no session holds either key [CNF-20, STA-17, SEC-1].
- [ ] The old key is removed only after a connection authenticated by the new one, and a failed confirmation leaves it in place [CNF-20].
- [ ] An interrupted migration is never reported complete [CNF-20, CNF-84 (partial Replace)].
- [ ] The old pass is not shown retired before the publisher's confirmation is recorded, and an interrupted retirement is reported incomplete, separately from machine migration [CNF-20 (relay half), STA-17].
- [ ] The screen names application-secret rotation at its service, the unrevocable inference account credential, and possible thief persistence with a destroy-or-rebuild offer, and never describes re-arming as a remedy [CNF-20].
- [ ] Replace ends with the new seed's sheet, which a later import accepts and the old sheet no longer matches; machines show as having no current sheet until it is saved [CNF-20, STA-17].
- [ ] After Replace with a fresh seed, allocation works again [CNF-84].
- [ ] Replace passes a freshly generated seed to the core, and a test shows that a Replace to a seed used before cannot reissue an identity; nothing relies on the core's guard as a freshness check [STA-17, STA-22b] (from twr-ggw.59).

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.27 — Exporting and importing the recovery sheet

## Spec
STA-17, SEC-1, ADR-0040, CNF-20, CNF-84

title: The paid-tcp-relay handshake matrix on the relay fixture
description:
## What to build
The relay fixture grows paid-tcp-relay's full handshake, and the harness's relay client passes CNF-87's handshake items against it. These are the fixture half of CNF-87; the same test set runs against the publisher's relay in twr-ggw.26.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A stale challenge, an unknown key and a replayed signature are each refused [CNF-87, WIR-4–WIR-10].
- [ ] Only the recorded destination set is reachable, and the relay's timing limits from the bundle are applied [CNF-87].
- [ ] The order challenge, AUTH, OK holds; a binary frame before OK, or a text frame after it, closes the socket [CNF-87].
- [ ] The fixture records no dial before the AUTH is accepted and no byte before OK [CNF-87].
- [ ] The client signs with a relay key the test supplies; twr-ggw.11 replaces it with the derived relay key.

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.2 — Tracer bullet: one recorded command over a pinned SSH connection through a relay fixture

## Spec
CHN-15, CHN-16, WIR-4–WIR-10, CNF-87

title: An unfinished setup owns the first screen; abandonment where the vendor offers no destroy route
description:
## What to build
Resume-or-abandon is the opening screen, with what has been billed and what bills monthly. Abandonment is the deterministic operator flow, outside any session: it destroys through typed operations where the vendor offers the operator a destroy route, and on a fixture adapter with stop, renewal control and reinstall but no destroy it applies ARC-22's treatment. A Restore that finds a cloud machine with no sheet offers that treatment, never an unpinned login.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The opening screen is resume-or-abandon, with billed-so-far and the monthly cost [ARC-22].
- [ ] Abandonment runs as the deterministic operator flow, never through a session, and against a machine with an unresolved call it is a disposition [ARC-21, STA-24].
- [ ] On the no-destroy fixture adapter it stops the machine, turns renewal off and shows it as "still existing and billed until the vendor's stated deletion date" [ARC-22].
- [ ] It names an unresolved create that no listing matches as possibly still existing and billing, and the listing runs as a read [ARC-22, STA-24].

title: ARC-33's policy and the harness worker: does it bind the worker's context, and how does a static host deliver it?
description:
## The gap

`ARC-33` sets the Content-Security-Policy that is "the boundary for code the harness never
meant to run": strict `script-src`, `object-src` and `base-uri`, permissive `connect-src`. It
does not say whether that policy must also bind the harness worker's own context. Nor does it
say how a static host delivers the policy to the worker (`ARC-32`: "served from a single
origin, as a static HTTPS host").

The two cases behave differently:

- **Page.** The served build (twr-ggw.2, commit 55dedb4) carries the policy in the page's
  `<meta>` element. That needs no host configuration.
- **Worker.** A dedicated worker loaded from an `https:` URL takes its policy from its own
  response headers, not from the page. A static host that sends no `Content-Security-Policy`
  header therefore leaves the harness worker with no policy at all. The harness worker is the
  context that holds keys, pins and the journal (`STA-1`, `STA-23`). The tracer only shows the
  policy enforced in the worker because its test server sends the header on `worker.js`. The
  README states this limit.

## The question for the specification

Does `ARC-33`'s policy bind the harness worker's context?
- **If it does:** how is it delivered from a static host? For example, a host configuration
  the repository ships, or a requirement on the host to send the header.
- **If it does not:** the corpus should say so, and say why the page's policy is enough.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The specification answers the question above, at a pin this repository adopts.
- [ ] The served build, or its documented deployment, follows that answer, with a check that
  fails when it does not.

title: The harness's relay client passes a text frame received after OK to SSH as bytes: does paid-tcp-relay's WIR-8 bind the client?
description:
## The gap

After the relay's `{"ok": true}`, the harness's relay client (`src/harness/run.rs`, from
twr-ggw.2 and twr-ggw.3, commit a0855f7) hands the WebSocket to SSH with ws_stream_wasm's
`into_io()`. In ws_stream_wasm 0.7.5, `From<WsMessage> for Vec<u8>` turns `WsMessage::Text(s)`
into its bytes. So a **text** frame the relay sends after OK enters the SSH byte stream as if it
were TCP bytes. Nothing ends the attempt.

paid-tcp-relay's `WIR-8` at `844e834` (the wire `CHN-15` adopts) says: "After `OK`, every frame in
both directions MUST be a binary frame carrying raw TCP. A text frame after `OK`, or a binary
frame before it, MUST close the connection with code 1002."

The impact is bounded. The SSH session is pinned end to end, so injected bytes can break the
session but cannot be accepted as the machine's. That is a denial of service, which a hostile
relay can already cause. What the harness lacks is conformance and a clear failure.

## The question

`CNF-87` and twr-ggw.3's matrix test the **relay** side of `WIR-8`. Does `WIR-8` also bind the
client? A browser cannot close with 1002 at all: `WebSocket.close()` accepts only 1000 or
3000–4999.
- **If it binds the client:** the harness must end the attempt on a text frame after OK, and the
  wire must say what a browser closes with.
- **If it does not:** paid-tcp-relay should say so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The question above is answered upstream (paid-tcp-relay), at a pin this repository adopts.
- [ ] If the client is bound: the harness ends the attempt on a text frame after OK and does not
  pass its bytes to SSH. A tracer case shows it, with the relay fixture made to send such a
  frame.

title: The CNF-13 source scan does not see a key held in a union or under a renamed import
description:
## The gap

twr-ggw.4 added `CNF-13`'s source scan (`src/credential.rs`, the tests module). It reads every
file under `src/` with `syn` and fails on a type that holds key material by its field types but
implements no `Credential`, so no `SEC-5` row. Two forms of key-holding type pass it unseen:

- **A union.** `visit_item_union` counts the union's name for the ambiguity rule, but always
  records it as holding no key. `union U { k: [u8; 32] }` in `src/` leaves the scan green.
- **A key type under another name.** Key types are matched by the last path segment
  (`SigningKey`, `SecretKey`, `PrivateKey`, …). `use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey as Sk;
  struct A(Sk);` leaves the scan green.

Neither form exists in `src/` today, so nothing is missed now. The scan is documented as a
guardrail, not a proof: it already cannot see a key carried in a `String` or a `Vec<u8>`. But the
module doc, the README and the scan's own doc say it fails on "a type that holds key material by
its field types". A union is such a type, and a renamed import is such a field type.

## The question

Should the guardrail cover these two forms, or should its documentation name them as outside it,
as it names `String` and `Vec<u8>`?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Either the scan reports a union holding key material, and a key type imported under another
  name, each shown by the planted-text test; or the scan's doc and the README name both forms as
  unseen.

title: The seed-backup ceremony STA-23 names has no owning ticket, and the store's seed is shown nowhere
description:
## The gap

twr-ggw.5 (commit 37e8161) creates the local store with a seed generated inside the harness
worker, and keeps its mnemonic in the store's first, encrypted record. Nothing displays it: spec
`STA-23` says "The mnemonic may be displayed only in the dedicated seed-backup ceremony, outside
session/model context", and no ticket under this epic builds that ceremony. A search of every
ticket's title and description for "seed-backup", "seed backup" and "backup ceremony" finds none.

Until one exists, an operator who creates a store holds a seed they have never seen. `STA-22`
says the seed is "backed up by the operator the way this audience already backs up seeds", and
`SEC-5` row 15 places it "in the operator's head or seed backup". A lost store or a forgotten
local passphrase then loses the seed for good, and every key derived from it. That costs nothing
today, because nothing derives a machine's key from the seed yet. It costs every maintained
machine once binding (twr-ggw.11) and allocation (twr-ggw.6) use the seed.

The specification names the ceremony and says nothing else about it: not when it runs, not
whether setup waits for a confirmed backup, and not whether the operator must prove the backup,
for example by re-entering words.

## The question

Which ticket owns the seed-backup ceremony, and does the specification need to say more about it
before it is built, such as when it runs and what completes it?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A ticket owns the seed-backup ceremony, and it is ordered before the first ticket that
  derives a key the operator relies on from the seed.
- [ ] Any question the specification leaves open about the ceremony is taken to the specification
  repository first.

title: An imported seed must not allocate after a restart or an interrupted import, and Replace must take a fresh seed
description:
## The gap

twr-ggw.6 (commit 22a6dde) puts `STA-22b`'s restriction in the allocation core, and nowhere
else. A restore is an ordinary core event, and the restriction is part of the core's state. The
store replays a restore record of its own seed. But no store method writes one, and no store can
yet be created from an imported seed: that durable import path is twr-ggw.27's. `STA-22b` says
"a seed imported after loss of the canonical journal may restore listed identities but MUST NOT
allocate new ones", and "This restriction also applies to an imported local-store backup".

twr-ggw.27's criterion reads "A stale sheet or an imported store cannot allocate under the
restored seed". Four behaviours that criterion does not pin, each of which can reissue or lose an
identity:

1. **A restart.** The restriction holds only if it is journaled. A test that allocates once,
   in the same worker, passes even when the restriction lives only in memory. Lock, reload, page
   hide and a killed worker each restart the worker and replay the journal (twr-ggw.5). So the
   check must restart the worker and replay before it tries to allocate.
2. **An interrupted import.** Replay builds an unrestricted, fresh-seed allocation state from
   record 0's seed (`src/store.rs`, `Metadata::new(seed.id())`). And unlocking an envelope with no
   record finishes creation by generating a new seed (`Store::finish_creation`). Two failures
   follow:
   - An import that commits the imported seed's record and dies before the record carrying the
     restriction leaves a store that allocates under the imported seed.
   - An import that dies after the envelope falls through to a freshly generated seed.

   Each must reopen refused or incomplete, never as a store that allocates.
3. **Where a restore record may sit.** Replay applies a restore record of the store's own seed at
   any position. That replaces the entries and counters with the export's, so identities the
   journal recorded after that export vanish from the metadata. Allocation is barred until a
   Replace, so none is reissued under that seed. But a later sheet export would omit them.
4. **Replace's freshness.** The core refuses a Replace only to the current seed or to one an
   entry names. After a restore drops a later seed's entries, a Replace back to that seed is
   accepted and reissues its identities. `STA-17`'s Replace says "generate a **new seed**", so
   twr-ggw.29 must pass a freshly generated one, and nothing may rely on the core's guard as a
   freshness check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The import path journals the restriction. After a worker restart and replay, allocation is
  refused in every family, under a test that restarts the worker [STA-22b].
- [ ] An import killed at each storage operation reopens refused or incomplete. It never reopens
  as a store that allocates, and never falls through to a freshly generated seed [STA-22b].
- [ ] Replay refuses a restore record anywhere the import path does not put it, unless the owner
  decides otherwise.
- [ ] Replace passes a freshly generated seed to the core, and a test shows that a Replace to a
  seed used before cannot reissue an identity [STA-17, STA-22b].

title: Allocation: an index is journaled before use and never reused
description:
## What to build
Per-family monotonic counters with consumed tombstones: an index is reserved durably before any external effect, and a reservation that produced no machine stays consumed. The journal refuses a machine at a recorded index, and a seed imported without its journal allocates nothing. The allocation core runs the companion comparison against the allocation witness file.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Deriving twice from the same seed and index gives identical keys, and the journal refuses to create a machine at a recorded index [CNF-72, STA-22].
- [ ] A reservation is journaled before any external effect, and a tombstoned index is never issued again [STA-22b].
- [ ] A seed imported after loss of the canonical journal restores the listed identities and allocates no new one [STA-22b].
- [ ] The allocation core passes the companion comparison against the allocation witness file at the spec pin, and CNF-3's three breaks each turn it red, naming the trace; the breaks are made once by hand and recorded here [CNF-3, ADR-0032].

comments.text:
Done in 22a6dde (feat: journal each allocation before use and never reuse an index). It took two rloop Rounds, and every reviewer on the four-model Panel accepted Round 2.

**What was built:**
- **The allocation core**, `src/allocation.rs`. It is pure and built on every target.
  - It holds STA-22b's allocation metadata, with a monotonic counter per family: machines, passes and handoffs.
  - Failed and destroyed entries are tombstones. They are never revived, and their index is never reissued.
  - No index past 2^31-1 is issued, and the counters never wrap.
  - Restore is an ordinary core event. It refuses allocation in every family until a Replace.
- **Journaling in the local store.**
  - Store::allocate takes no index. The reservation is appended, applied once committed, and only then returned (STA-3).
  - Replay applies each record through the same core. It fails closed on a recorded or skipped index, an unknown version, an allocation under the restriction, an inapplicable observation, a replace record, or a restore of another seed's metadata (CNF-72).

**Criteria:**
- **AC1, CNF-72 and STA-22.** The same keys re-derive after a reopen, and the journal refuses a machine at a recorded index, through the API and at replay.
- **AC2, STA-22b.** The commit lands before the identity is returned. A failed append, a move that lands and then reports failure, a kill after the commit, and tombstones across a reopen are each tested.
- **AC3, STA-22b.** The seed's mnemonic is imported after the store is discarded and the core's export is restored. The listed identities and their keys come back, and allocation is refused in all three families until a Replace with a fresh seed. The same refusal holds through a journaled restore record, after replay.
- **AC4, CNF-3 and ADR-0032.** The comparison reads spec/docs/design/allocation-witnesses-v1.json from the pinned tree at run time. Its record:
  - file: spec/docs/design/allocation-witnesses-v1.json; schema 1, module allocation;
  - bound: 3 events over an alphabet of 7;
  - compared: 6 witnesses and 400 enumerated traces, every step;
  - pair: TauWeb.Allocation.stale_sheet_refused matched, and TauWeb.Allocation.stale_sheet_admitted differed at step 7, the negative control;
  - spec commit: 1cc84987d76a5e9237e9e8a09287dc5e9e4c5ac4;
  - implementation revision: 22a6dde.

  The comparison also checks that the enumeration is complete for its bound, that every enumerated trace starts from the initial journal, and that the pair names itself both ways. Anything unknown fails, naming its trace.

**CNF-3's three breaks, made once by hand on 2026-10-12.** The comparison test's path was edited temporarily to a scratch copy outside spec/, since build.rs refuses a dirty spec/. It was green against the unmodified copy first.
1. **An outcome flipped**: TauWeb.Allocation.successful_trace, step 1, admitted changed to refused. Red: "TauWeb.Allocation.successful_trace, step 1 (allocate): allocation: expected refused, actual admitted".
2. **The file missing, then empty.** Red both times, naming the path:
   - "…/allocation-witnesses-v1.json: No such file or directory (os error 2)";
   - "…: not a JSON document: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0".
3. **Unrecognised input.** Red both times, naming the trace:
   - enumeration[1]'s event kind changed to "reallocate": "enumeration[1], step 1: event: unknown variant `reallocate`";
   - its outcome changed to "granted": "enumeration[1], step 1: unknown variant `granted`".

Both the copy and the path edit were restored, confirmed with cmp, and the test went green again. The same breaks stay as permanent unit tests on the comparator, alongside a truncated enumeration, an unknown member, a pair missing its admitted side, and an enumerated trace (empty, or with steps) that starts away from the initial journal. README "The gates" records the by-hand breaks too.

**Mutation proofs.** Each was made by hand and turned its named tests red, and each restore was confirmed with cmp:
- Round 1: allocation under the restriction; a failed index reissued; a failed entry revived; the exhaustion check removed; apply before commit; replay accepting a recorded identity; Replace leaving the restriction set.
- Round 2: the start check removed. Two reviewers reproduced this one independently.

**Consultation (pick).** The question was whether AC3 is realised on the core only, or through a store import path now. It settled on the core only, 3–1: fable, opus and astra for it, sol for the store path. Both vendors were in the majority. Durable import stays with twr-ggw.27. The record is in the Run's brief.

**Notes for later tickets:**
- **The tracer reader's needle check.** seed_secrets in tracer/src/reader.rs lists the seed identifier as a needle, and the reader test asserts that no decrypted record after record 0 holds one. An allocation record carries the seed identifier inside the encryption, where credential format v1 puts it. So the first ticket that writes allocation records into a store the reader reads will see that assertion go red, loudly. That ticket should exempt the identifier inside allocation records.

title: The operator's disposition act, and unresolved calls and dispositions on screen
description:
## What to build
The operator records a disposition by an act on the screen, outside any model path. For one resource, the operator names some or all of its unresolved calls (or, to replace the standing disposition, the calls it disposed), chooses one of the four continuations, and records the uncertainty accepted. The harness worker records it through the store's disposition test (`Store::dispose`, twr-ggw.7), and the screen shows what happened. The screen shows each resource's unresolved calls; its standing disposition and that disposition's continuation; every refused disposition, with what settled the call and what is unresolved now; what a replacement replaced; every disposition refused at replay; evidence that arrived after a disposition; and each request the barrier refused, with the call that refused it. twr-ggw.8 supplies the typed operations and the reports its criteria make for the operator's screen; pairing a refused request with the unresolved call that refused it is this ticket's, in the harness as on the screen.

Not this ticket's: dispatching a continuation (the abandonment flow is twr-ggw.31's, the stop that stands in for a destroy twr-ggw.40's, the reinstall twr-ggw.45's, the reset into rescue twr-i6k.3's); the model's tool result when a request is refused (twr-ggw.67); ARC-22's opening screen (twr-ggw.31); an unresolved inference request shown as unaccounted spend (twr-ggw.17); a sibling entry's approval card (twr-ggw.21); the screen's statement before a destructive choice under an untyped vendor scope (CNF-105, stage 2).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A disposition is recorded only by the operator's act on the screen: "Neither a timer nor the model supplies one", and of a replacement, "Neither a timer nor the model replaces one". Implementation reading: no model tool, harness job or timer reaches the act, and a test fails if any path other than the operator's act records a disposition [STA-24].
- [ ] The act names one resource; at least one call, each unresolved on that resource or, for a replacement, disposed by the standing disposition; one of the four continuations, "a destructive reinstall (`STG-20`), abandonment (`ARC-21`), continuing as if done, continuing as if not done"; and "the uncertainty accepted". The store's test decides it, and an accepted disposition is durably appended before it is applied [STA-24, STA-3].
- [ ] Each unresolved call is shown on the screen with its resource and what was requested (the box-plane command, or the typed operation's approved facts), as unresolved: it "is not reported as failed", and it is never shown as pending, in flight, failed or timed out [STA-8, CNF-29, CONTEXT.md "Unresolved"].
- [ ] A request refused because a call naming its resource is unresolved is shown on the screen with that unresolved call: "The request is refused and the unresolved call is shown in its place: to the model as the tool result, to the operator on the screen"; the model's half is twr-ggw.67's. Implementation reading: a request a standing disposition refuses is shown with that disposition and its continuation [STA-24].
- [ ] Each resource's standing disposition is shown with the calls it disposed, its continuation and the uncertainty accepted, and each disposed call's outcome is shown as unknown: "it is never written as success, failure, zero spend or non-execution" [STA-24].
- [ ] Under either continuation that continues, the screen shows the operator's recorded assumption, continuing as if done or continuing as if not done, "which is shown and never written as success, failure, zero spend or non-execution" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition that names no call, names a call already settled (by a terminal record, or by a disposition other than the standing one, whose calls only a replacement may name: "a new disposition may name the calls the standing one disposed"), or names a call on another resource records nothing, and the screen shows "that it was refused, the record that settled the call if one did, and what is unresolved now" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] After a disposition naming some of several unresolved calls, the screen shows the named calls under it and the others still unresolved: "the unnamed ones stay unresolved and keep their barrier" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] After a replacement, "the operator is shown what it replaces", and the screen shows the replacement's continuation as the one in force; with a destructive reinstall replaced by abandonment, abandonment is shown in force [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Once the continuation is dispatched, with its intent durably appended, the screen no longer shows the disposition as standing and shows that call instead: the disposition "stands until its continuation is dispatched or the operator replaces it", and "from then on that call's own barrier governs" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition in a replayed journal that the test refuses is shown as refused, and no call is shown as disposed by it: "it ends no call and restricts nothing, every call it named that is unresolved stays unresolved and keeps its barrier, and the operator is shown the record" [CNF-110, STA-24, STA-7].
- [ ] Evidence about a disposed call that arrives after its disposition is shown beside that call, which stays shown as disposed under the standing disposition: it "is journaled and shown: it neither reopens the call nor removes the disposition" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Nothing the screen receives for the act or the display carries key material, the seed or a credential the harness holds; the UI "never receives the unwrapped data key" [STA-23, SEC-5].
- [ ] Each criterion above has a test that fails when the act or the screen breaks it.

## Blocked by
- twr-ggw.7 — Box-plane commands go through the journal and survive a killed worker
- twr-ggw.8 — Typed operations on a fixture adapter, behind the unresolved barrier

STA-3, STA-7, STA-8, STA-23, STA-24, SEC-5, CNF-29, CNF-110

title: Typed operations on a fixture adapter, behind the unresolved barrier
description:
## What to build
A fixture adapter's reads, create and running-system changes are approved on structured facts, recorded before they are sent, and confirmed only by observable state. While one is unresolved, the barrier on its approved machine entry refuses the same effect however it is requested again, and a running-system change stops box-plane dispatch to that machine. The dispatch core runs the companion comparison over the dispatch witness traces that consult no rescue rule; twr-i6k.3 runs the rest.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Killing the worker between record and send leaves the record [CNF-28 (fixture adapter), SEC-12].
- [ ] A lost response to a fixture create leaves it unresolved; a second request for it under a new call id, through another tool, after replay or from a later session is refused, and so is a second allocation index for the same entry; a different approved entry stays permitted [CNF-29, STA-24].
- [ ] A read naming the resource stays permitted, and a status read whose journal append fails leaves the barrier standing [CNF-29, STA-24].
- [ ] A fixture reset or reinstall stops box-plane dispatch to that machine from its intent until its confirmation or a disposition [STA-24].
- [ ] Each operation is approved on its facts, never on command text [ARC-4].
- [ ] With a fixture call that changes what the machine is running left unresolved and disposed, a box-plane command to that machine is refused under a destructive reinstall and under abandonment: "A destructive continuation stops the model's commands" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Within the disposed calls' reach, every cloud-plane operation the continuation does not permit is refused: "A destructive reinstall permits only the reinstall, abandonment only the abandonment flow"; an operation outside that reach is neither restricted by it nor ends it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With a fixture call that changes what the machine is running left unresolved and disposed under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched, and the same operation requested again under a fresh call id is dispatched where no other call is unresolved: "Continuing as if done and continuing as if not done restrict nothing" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] For either continuation that continues, the harness reports the operator's recorded assumption for the operator's screen, "never written as success, failure, zero spend or non-execution"; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With an unresolved fixture create disposed to continue under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane"; this ticket exercises the create case [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With any stage-1 call disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, an unresolved box-plane command included, the model's box-plane command to that machine is refused, "whatever the disposed call was" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, a status read is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "A read and the inference request are never restricted"; a model's command refused before the read is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Across CNF-110's stage-1 disposition cases, a pinned SSH attempt is dispatched and does not end the restriction: "Reads stay permitted throughout"; a model's command refused before the attempt is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] For stage-1 continuations, the restriction ends at the dispatch of the reinstall or of the destroy (the stop that stands in for one), its intent durably appended, and not before: "from then on that call's own barrier governs"; from that intent the call's own barrier refuses and nothing is refused under the disposition [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition naming no call, a call already settled or a call on another resource is refused and journals nothing; the harness reports for the operator's screen "the refusal, the record that settled the call if one did, and what is unresolved now"; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A disposition naming some of several unresolved calls leaves the others barring: "the unnamed ones stay unresolved and keep their barrier" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A replacement naming the calls the standing disposition disposed is accepted, and the harness reports what it replaces for the operator's screen: "One disposition stands per resource, the latest, and its continuation is the one in force"; with a destructive reinstall replaced by abandonment, the reinstall is refused; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A replayed journal already holding a disposition that the naming test refuses, the replacement exception included, "ends no call and restricts nothing"; calls it named that remain unresolved keep their barrier, and the harness reports the refused record for the operator's screen; rendering on screen is twr-ggw.66's [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] A valid replacement is still the one in force after a worker restart and journal replay: "the continuation in force after a restart is the latest valid one" [CNF-110, STA-24, STA-7].
- [ ] Evidence appended after a disposition about a call it disposed is journaled and reported and "neither reopens the call nor removes the disposition"; the disposition stands until its continuation is dispatched or the operator replaces it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] The dispatch core passes the companion comparison over every trace of `dispatch-witnesses-v2.json` that consults no rescue rule, routed by one step test written in the test: a trace goes to twr-i6k.3 iff it holds a `reset_prereqs` step, a request or read of `activate` or `register_key`, or a `reset` request after a `destructive_reinstall` disposition, reading `start`'s dispositions and `reset_offer` as records before the first step (a non-empty `reset_offer` counts as `reset_prereqs`); every other trace is this ticket's (24 witnesses and 227 enumerated traces at `ee133d0`; twr-i6k.3's are listed as left to it, each refused/admitted pair whole). This ticket's traces hold requests to create, exec, reset, reinstall, destroy (the stop that stands in for one), read and inference; dispositions to `abandonment` and `destructive_reinstall`, recorded or refused; adapter reads of a reset or a reinstall; and replay. A schema other than 2, or an event kind, operation, continuation, source or outcome neither ticket names, fails, naming the trace. title: The rescue ceremony: a host-key pin at both hops, rescue job records and the blocked append
description:
## What to build
The rescue system's host-key pin is read from the vendor after the reset, per boot, and nothing connects before it is published; the ready-to-reset job journals the installed system's host-key pins before the reset is offered, and a key the model emits never becomes a pin. Rescue jobs are never launched twice within a boot, and with the journal append blocked no reset is offered or dispatched; once the append is allowed, records and pins are recovered and dispatch resumes on the reset's confirmation. The dispatch core runs the companion comparison over the dispatch witness traces twr-ggw.8 left.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The rescue host-key pin is read from the vendor after the reset and before the first connection, and the activation response is never a host-key source [CNF-22, STG-4].
- [ ] The installed system's host-key pins come from the ready-to-reset job's own output, and a different key the model emits in its text is not pinned [CNF-22, ARC-43].
- [ ] CNF-38's four cases pass [CNF-38, STG-11].
- [ ] With SSH dropped during partitioning, the returning session reads the same rescue boot's job and does not duplicate it, including under a new command id [CNF-86, STA-20b].
- [ ] With the journal append blocked before the planned reboot, no reset is offered and none dispatched, including through a separately requested typed operation; once allowed, records and pins are recovered and dispatch resumes on the reset's confirmation, not on reconnection [CNF-86, STA-20b].
- [ ] An unexpected rescue reboot leaves the old command unresolved until inspection or a disposition [CNF-86].
- [ ] With an unresolved Robot activation or key registration disposed under either continuation that continues, a box-plane command is dispatched: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane"; this ticket exercises the activation and key-registration cases [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] With an unresolved Robot activation disposed toward a destructive reinstall or abandonment, the model's box-plane command to that machine is refused, "whatever the disposed call was" [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] While a destructive-reinstall disposition stands, the rescue activation and a key registration where one is owed "are admitted and do not end the restriction"; the model's command refused before either is still refused after it [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Under a standing destructive-reinstall disposition, a reset with no confirmed rescue activation is refused: "Any other reset is refused while the disposition stands"; the disposition and its restriction remain standing [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] After rescue activation confirmation, a reset whose newest journaled activation read reports it inactive is refused with the disposition still standing: "A read that does not confirm the activation, inactive or one that tells nothing, leaves it not counted"; the activation call stays terminal [CNF-110, STA-24].
- [ ] Immediately before the reset into rescue dispatches a standing disposition's destructive reinstall, "the harness MUST read the activation predicate again and durably journal the read"; only a re-read the journal holds discharges the duty. After a re-read confirming the activation, the reset is admitted and ends the restriction at its durably appended intent; from that intent its own barrier governs, and nothing is refused under the disposition [CNF-110, STA-24, STG-4].
- [ ] Evidence appended after a disposition "neither reopens the call nor removes the disposition"; a read of the rescue activation decides which reset counts, using the newest journaled activation-predicate read before the reset's intent, never `/rescue/last`, and "reopens nothing and removes nothing" [CNF-110, STA-24].

## What

Publisher, paying one month at LNVPS.

T39 is closed on the spec's main: phase B's ordered observations are recorded, LNVPS passes the stage-1 target criteria, and the route is admitted.
